paper.title: Can an Embodied Agent Find Your "Cat-shaped Mug"? LLM-Guided Exploration for Zero-Shot Object Navigation
paper.central_claim: LGX (Language-guided Exploration) combines GPT-3 commonsense decisions about where to explore, taken from detector object labels or image captions, with GLIP open-vocabulary grounding to solve language-driven zero-shot object navigation (L-ZSON): state-of-the-art RoboTHOR results (over 27% SR improvement over OWL CoW), a study of prompt strategies, and the first real-world L-ZSON evaluation on a TurtleBot.
paper.scope_decision: in_scope (borderline): frozen GPT-3 chooses exploration targets from detector labels inside a navigation loop with GLIP stop gate and ROS motion, in RoboTHOR and on a TurtleBot 2.

preliminary_judgment: Written after reading the fixed text, before opening this paper's seat records: system_method; RoboTHOR val 1800 episodes single run; LGX 35.0 vs GoW 33.2 vs OWL-CoW 27.5 (quoted): LLM adds +1.8, grounder swap +5.7; G_th tuned on the reported set; target-in-view criterion; prompt study on best/worst subset; real world 54.2/27.8/6.9 without counts and staged phase-2 LLM inputs; no cost. Expected online, scoped, weak holdout/statistics.

evidence.support_explanation: Original comparative claim; percentage is relative to OWL-CoW, not isolated LLM gain.

evidence.quote: we first extract contextual cues from the scene in the form of object labels or scene captions. Either of these cues are then used to devise a prompt asking the LLM about which how the agent should proceed to explore the environment. The LLM uses its commonsense knowledge about object relationships in the environment to provide the agent with a direction or object for it to move towards. Simultaneously, we use a Vision-Language model, GLIP [ 17 ] to obtain a target object grounding s
evidence.support_explanation: Scene-to-text context conditions frozen LLM direction/object choices; no task-specific retraining.

evidence.quote: An episode is rendered successful if the target object is in the agent’s view while performing rotate-in-place.
evidence.support_explanation: Explicit visual target criterion, not a conventional distance-arrival guarantee.

evidence.quote: It contains 1800 validation episodes with 15 validation environments. 12 different goal object categories are present. Each exploratory turn carries out the scene understanding procedure described earlier in sections III-B and III-C . For each episode, we run LGX for n_{r} exploratory turns or until it detects the target object above the G_{th} threshold. These constraints form the STOP condition. n_{r} is set to 5, given the small environments in RoboTHOR, where the target object is usually within 10 meters of the spawning point. G_{th} is set to 0.85 for RoboTHOR after ablation experiments described in Table I . The exploratory distance e_{d} described in III-D is set to 5 m, ensuring significant changes to the scenery in RoboTHOR after motion. G_{th} SR (%) SPL (%)

signatures.object: Exploration decision module: GPT-3 chooses which detected object (or which of four directions) to head towards.
signatures.information: After a 360-degree rotate-in-place, the LLM sees a text prompt with YOLO class labels (or BLIP captions per 90 degrees) and the target description; it does not see the map, history or the images themselves.
signatures.operation: Prompt template 'You are controlling a home robot ... Which object from {O} should the robot go towards?' (7 prompt variants studied); the answer reorients the robot, a random cost-map point 5 m ahead is picked and move_base drives there; invalid answers trigger a random direction.
signatures.output: Heading / sub-goal for a ROS navigation stack.
signatures.conditions: RGB-D rotation each step, n_r = 5 turns in RoboTHOR, closed-set detector classes.
signatures.feedback: none from the LLM's own earlier choices (no memory)
signatures.claimed_effect: +1.8 SR / +1.6 SPL over GLIP-on-Wheels in simulation; 54.2% vs 27.8% in the staged real-world test.
signatures.failure_boundary: LLM associates a target with the wrong co-occurring object (desk/Red Bull can, jacket/desk); loops with caption prompts; RoboTHOR weak testbed (authors).

signatures.object: Open-vocabulary grounding and stop gate: GLIP run on every rotation image with the free-form target phrase.
signatures.information: RGB images and the language target; GLIP confidence threshold G_th = 0.85.
signatures.operation: Stop and declare the target found when GLIP confidence exceeds G_th; otherwise continue exploring up to n_r turns.
signatures.output: STOP signal; success judged by simulator truth that the target is in view.
signatures.conditions: Threshold chosen by SR on the validation split that is reported; detector chosen after comparing several detectors qualitatively (Fig 8).
signatures.selection_rule: threshold G_th picked by maximum SR (Table I)
signatures.claimed_effect: GoW (GLIP only) 33.2 SR vs OWL-CoW 27.5 SR, i.e. grounding model change explains most of the headline gain.
signatures.failure_boundary: GLIP false negatives for stevia packets, false positives for Red Bull can in real-world tests (Fig 6-7).

gap.author_gap: L-ZSON needs navigation to uniquely described objects in unseen environments; supervised ObjectNav does not cover free-form language; FBE exploration is uninformed; no L-ZSON method had been evaluated in the real world.
gap.checked_gap: Grounding gap supported (OWL-CoW 27.5 vs GLIP-based GoW 33.2 on the same exploration policy). Exploration gap is asserted: the LLM adds only +1.8 SR over GoW in simulation and the authors concede RoboTHOR is a skewed basis for it. Real-world gap is a genuine contribution but the real test is staged.
lineage: CoW (FBE + CLIP) and OWL-CoW (FBE + OWL-ViT) [3] -> GLIP-on-Wheels (FBE + GLIP, authors' ablation) -> LGX (LLM-chosen direction/object + GLIP); LLM planners (Huang et al., SayCan) and LM-Nav / VLMaps are described as different roles and not compared
gap.closest_adjacent: CoW / OWL-CoW numbers are quoted from [3]; GoW is re-run by the authors. No empirical comparison with other LLM navigation systems (LM-Nav, VLMaps, ZSON).
gap.residue: Whether commonsense co-occurrence from a closed-set label list improves exploration efficiency over frontier exploration once the grounding model is controlled.
gap.stakes: Navigation to uncommon objects in new homes (SR/SPL on RoboTHOR; two-room real course).
gap.method_response: LLM chooses among detected labels or four directions each step; GLIP supplies grounding and the stop test.
gap.remaining_gap: LLM benefit small and single-run in simulation; no history; closed-set YOLO labels limit the LLM's view of unique objects; real-world evidence staged and without trial counts.
gap.current_relevance: Not assessed from later work; no later paper in the pinned local set bears on it.
unresolved: Whether baseline numbers from [3] share the same success criterion as the view-based criterion used here.
LLM engine and decoding settings are not stated.

claims.text: LLM commonsense improves exploration decisions and prompt design matters.
claims.setting: Seven prompt variants on a subset of 500 best/worst episodes; YOLO vs BLIP front-ends
claims.baseline_control: GoW; random direction only in the real world
claims.selection_vs_test: prompt study on selected episodes of the same validation split
claims.result_denominator: SR 28.1-33.8 across prompts while PSR ranges 52.3-100; one run
counterevidence: authors state RoboTHOR is a skewed basis for this
claims.allowed_conclusion: Object-label prompts work better than caption prompts; prompt wording changes validity rate (PSR) much more than success.

claims.text: LGX works in the real world and beats GLIP-on-Wheels and random exploration.
claims.setting: TurtleBot 2, two-phase course (room -> hallway -> correct room), four rooms with staged target and common objects
claims.selection_vs_test: scenario designed by the authors; LLM input per room staged from Table II
claims.result_denominator: 54.2% vs 27.8% vs 6.9% (counts not reported; percentages imply about 72 trials); 20.8% Phase-2 failure; GLIP TP 87.5%, FP 8.3%
counterevidence: LLM chooses only among closed-set labels; phase-2 inputs hand-specified
claims.allowed_conclusion: In a staged two-room course LGX chose the right route more often than frontier-style and random baselines; not a measure of general L-ZSON success.

assessment.evidence_level_reason: Closed-loop RoboTHOR success judged by simulator truth; real-robot results lack trial counts and use staged LLM inputs; threshold tuned on the reported split. No transfer.
assessment.author_claim_preserved: LGX (Language-guided Exploration) combines GPT-3 commonsense decisions about where to explore, taken from detector object labels or image captions, with GLIP open-vocabulary grounding to solve language-driven zero-shot object navigation (L-ZSON): state-of-the-art RoboTHOR results (over 27% SR improvement over OWL CoW), a study of prompt strategies, and the first real-world L-ZSON evaluation on a TurtleBot.
assessment.strongest_supported_claim: On RoboTHOR validation (1800 episodes, one run), swapping the grounder to GLIP gives most of the improvement over OWL-CoW (27.5 -> 33.2 SR), and adding GPT-3 heading selection over YOLO labels adds a further +1.8 SR/+1.6 SPL with a stop threshold tuned on that same split; the claim that LLM-guided exploration explains the 27% gain is not supported.
unresolved: Success-criterion equivalence with quoted CoW baselines
assessment.reproduction: author_report only; no reproduction by us

G.reason: Resolved toward son55 (sol 3). The grounding gap is real and supported (OWL-CoW 27.5 -> GoW 33.2 with the same frontier exploration), but the paper's own contribution is the exploration gap, which is asserted rather than located: GoW already reaches 33.2, LM-Nav/VLMaps/ZSON are described not compared, and the authors concede RoboTHOR is a skewed basis for context-dependent exploration. Anchor 2: real limitation, incomplete residual.

M.reason: Resolved toward son55 (sol 3). Concrete mechanism (rotate, YOLO labels, LLM picks a label/direction, GLIP stops) with a commonsense co-occurrence rationale and a distinguishable prediction vs frontier exploration, but key assumptions are thin: the LLM chooses only among closed-set labels (agg:E003), has no visit history (loops reported), invalid outputs fall back to a random direction, and the 'mapless' rationale conflicts with the costmap step (agg:E002). Anchor 2: mechanism with partial causal story, weak key assumptions.

X.reason: Resolved toward son55 (sol 3). Main steps and prompts are given, but conditions needed to reproduce or bound the result are missing: GPT-3 engine/decoding, YOLO-branch rotation resolution, GoW/FBE budgets and threshold, whether quoted CoW numbers share the target-in-view success criterion, and the real-world phase-2 LLM input is a staged object list rather than live detections. Anchor 2: main steps described, key conditions unclear.

measurement.reason: Both 2; confirmed. Simulator-truth target-in-view success over 1800 episodes, but the criterion differs from stop-near-goal ObjectNav, CoW/OWL-CoW numbers are quoted from [3], and real-world denominators are unstated.

causality.reason: Both 2; confirmed. GoW isolates the LLM exploration with the grounder fixed: +1.8 SR / +1.6 SPL, single run with a threshold tuned on the same set; BLIP variant below GoW; the abstract's 27% is mostly the grounder swap (27.5 -> 33.2).

holdout.reason: Both 1; confirmed. Stop threshold chosen on the reported validation split (agg:E001), prompt study on best/worst episodes of that split, no separate test set, staged real-world inputs.

statistics.reason: Both 1; confirmed. Single run, no variance/CI, 'no significant difference' without a test; real-world phase failure shares and GLIP FP/FN without counts.

cost.reason: Revised (sol 2, son55 0/not_reported). Not not_reported: the exploration cap (n_r = 5 turns, e_d = 5 m) bounds LGX at five LLM queries per episode, which is applicable partial budget evidence (son55:E029, sol:E004). Not 2: unlike the anchor-2 instance and DEPS in this batch, the comparators' budgets (FBE/GoW steps, thresholds) are not stated, so budget fairness cannot be judged, and no call/latency/time figures exist. Placed at 1 on the anchor scale for these reasons, not by averaging the seats.

resolutions.reason: Exploration residual (the paper's own contribution) not located; grounder residual is inherited from the detector swap.
Closed-set label choice, no history, random fallback, 'mapless' inconsistency.
Engine/decoding, baseline budgets and success-criterion equivalence unknown; staged real-world inputs.
Turn cap is partial budget evidence (rules out not_reported); missing comparator budgets rule out the anchor-2 band. See rating reason.

The exploration/grounding/motion decomposition is inherited unchanged from CoW/GoW (the closest neighbours run the same split), so it is not the paper's differentiating operation. What LGX changes is the exploration decision: a new free-form target plus current scene labels are expressed as prompt conditioning to a frozen LLM, solved at inference without training (sol:E002, agg:E003). The decomposition is executed and structures the stop gate, so decompose_and_delegate is kept as supporting with sub_id null (C25 needs a verifiable artifact closing the loop; the LLM choice has no checker).
Both seats leave the sub null for their chosen card: C03 needs an upstream schema-parsing phase or reference substrate (absent); C25 needs verification closure (absent).

K104 and K109 agreed. K202 kept from sol as partial: GLIP confidence acts as a completion monitor that ends exploration and each 5 m step hands control back to the LLM decision; not K201 (no LLM proposal is gated). son55's unassigned 'LLM as semantic search prior over detected labels' and its pending proposal are retained.
No calls/tokens/latency/USD; only the turn cap (credited in E.cost).

The R2R-CE split requirement does not fit RoboTHOR ObjectNav (sol's challenge accepted), but the expectation's 'do not mix incomparable numbers' part applies: CoW/OWL-CoW numbers are quoted from [3] while LGX uses a target-in-view criterion whose equivalence is not shown.

shared_error_corrections.seats_value: Both scoped and both attribute most of the 27% to the GLIP swap.
shared_error_corrections.correction: Confirmed; added that the LLM only chooses among closed-set YOLO labels (agg:E003) and that the paper's 'mapless' exploration claim conflicts with its costmap step (agg:E002). Scope answered: in scope as a navigation harness with perception tools and an external stop gate, borderline because the LLM's role is a single label choice.
